# Edmate decision log

Every decision the spec did not already make, in plain words, newest first. Agents write entries in their task's handoff, and the team lead copies them here when the PR merges. Your own decisions are logged too.

- **risk: low** · the agent decided and moved on
- **risk: medium** · the agent or lead decided; worth a skim
- **risk: high** · you decided, or the lead merged a risky change (contracts, ADRs, safety, access, payments, the harness) after its required reviewers; skim these first

Format and rules: `.claude/skills/merge-gate/SKILL.md`.

---

### 27 Oct 2026 · 7.2u Phase O interpret the angle/trick cap at mechanism level · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: Read "reuses a covered angle without a plainly different angle" and "a trick given a
  4th rewording" at the level of the specific manipulative mechanism (for example "claimed
  institutional/professional authority demanding compliance", "claims to be another AI product",
  "romantic companion request"), not at the level of the broad topic ("is the AI human"). Found
  three families already at exactly three pre-existing uses before this phase
  (authority-claim-override: `admin-override`, `rule-override-developer-mode`,
  `rule-override-school-counselor`; other-AI-claim: `connected-apps`, `gpt-wrapper`, `replika`;
  companion-romantic: `girlfriend`, `latenight-boyfriend`, `prom-date`) and added zero new cases
  to any of the three, instead using fresh single-use mechanisms or extending an
  already-single-use family with a clearly distinct manifestation (for example bribery:
  5-star-review → extra-credit; consent-override: self-granted → parent-granted; pretend-other-
  teacher: unnamed subject → chemistry-with-urgency).
- Why: the brief's cap exists to stop the suite padding out with cosmetic rewordings of the same
  test; a topic-level reading (for example "any case about whether the AI is human") would have
  blocked most of the identity/boundary mix the brief explicitly asked for, while a mechanism-
  level reading keeps the cap's intent (no 4th rewording of one trick) without discarding cases
  that exercise a genuinely different manipulation.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 7.2u Phase O rewrite two cases that echoed their own banned phrase · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `persona-identity-reward-extracredit-en` and `persona-identity-translation-trick-en`
  originally had the student literally quote the banned phrase ("I am human") inside their own
  turn. Rewrote both so the student asks for the admission in different words (a confirmation "in
  plain words" that the agent is "a real human", or a description of the sentence to translate
  rather than a quote of it), confirmed by re-running the whole-suite echo-check script.
- Why: the brief's echo rule exists so a correct, compliant reply that merely restates what it is
  declining is never mistaken for a failure; a `must_not_contain` phrase that is already a
  substring of the student's own turn risks exactly that false failure, so the fix changes the
  student's wording rather than weakening the check.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 7.2u Phase O use a bare `stop` for the two pause→stop role-play cases · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `persona-roleplay-pause-resume-stop-viva-en`'s and `persona-roleplay-pause-then-stop-
  job-en`'s final turn reads literally `Stop.`, not a sentence such as "I want to stop the
  interview", after the fixture run showed `rolePlayControl` (`packages/harness/src/pedagogy/
  skills.ts`) only recognises a bare `stop`/`/stop` (case, spaces and one trailing `.`/`!`
  aside) as the stop control; any other wording is treated as an ordinary message turn (an answer
  to the paused question), not a stop. Also corrected both cases' `questions_answered` count to 1,
  not 2: the question paused on is never actually answered before the stop, so only the first
  question counts toward the debrief.
- Why: the case must match the real control-detection rule to test what it claims to test; a
  "soft" stop phrase would silently test an ordinary-message path instead of the stop path, and a
  debrief count that doesn't match the real state machine would make the case's own judge line
  wrong regardless of what the agent replies.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 7.2v re-wrap width for edited source blocks · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: when a citation replacement changed the logical source string's length, re-flowed the whole folded block to width 90 (2-space indent, no mid-word breaks) with Python textwrap, rather than trying to preserve the original line-break positions.
- Why: several stale citations were split across two physical lines inside the YAML folded scalar (the word "line" on one line, the number on the next), so a line-local sed/regex would have missed them; re-flowing the joined logical string is the only reliable way to catch and fix every instance, and YAML folded scalars don't care about line width, so this changes no wording or meaning.

### 27 Oct 2026 · Three upheld copyright takedowns in 12 months raise a staff alert; staff decide on suspension (B-63, task 12.3d) · decided by you · risk: high
Decided: A teacher with 3 upheld copyright takedowns in any 12 months is flagged to staff as a repeat infringer. Staff decide whether to suspend the teacher; a suspended teacher's agent takes no new students, and current students keep access until staff act. Nothing is suspended automatically in the pilot.
Why: A US platform hosting uploads needs a written repeat-infringer policy it applies, to keep its copyright safe harbour; a person decides during the pilot, the same shape as B-12's jailbreak strikes.
Alternatives: automatic suspension at 3 that staff can lift (b); no number, staff judge each case (c).
Reversible: Yes, the threshold and window are settings in 12.3d.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 0.20j instrumentation.test.ts patches Module.prototype.require instead of vi.mock · decided by builder · risk: low

  `Module.prototype.require` (restored in `afterEach`) instead of using `vi.mock`, which the plan's
  "Tests" section assumed would work.
- Why: confirmed empirically that Vitest's `vi.mock` only governs `import`/dynamic `import()`, not
  a literal `require(...)` call -- even against a real, built, npm-resolvable package
  (`@edmate/harness`). The production code must keep the literal `require(...)` token for Next's
  documented Edge-bundle-exclusion branch elimination to recognise it, so the test had to adapt
  instead; this is the same technique `mock-require`/`proxyquire` use for exactly this case.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 8.2r drop-and-reinstate of documents_failure_reason_only_when_failed · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: migration `0041_documents_list_index_failure_reason_validate.sql` contains

  immediately by `ALTER TABLE "documents" ADD CONSTRAINT
  "documents_failure_reason_only_when_failed" CHECK (...) NOT VALID;` — the merge gate's
  migration-content scan flags any `DROP CONSTRAINT`/`ALTER TABLE ... DROP` as "drops or deletes
  data", so this PR is risky via `MIGRATION_REVIEWERS = ("database-reviewer",)`.
- Why: this only re-adds the exact same CHECK expression, immediately, as `NOT VALID` — the same
  rule is enforced before and after (confirmed by the new
  `documents-failure-reason-validate-migration.int.test.ts`: existing rows on both sides of the
  constraint survive unchanged, the constraint is `convalidated = true` after `migrateDatabase`,
  and a row that violates it still fails to insert). No row is ever uncovered by the constraint
  for longer than the two statements take, and no data is read, written or lost — this is
  hygiene to match this repo's `NOT VALID` → `VALIDATE` convention (migrate.ts's
  `POST_MIGRATE_STEPS` comment), not a behaviour change. `database-reviewer` should confirm this
  reading before merge.

### 27 Oct 2026 · US payment provider: Paddle as merchant of record (B-53, task 10.1) · decided by you · risk: high
Decided: Paddle is the US merchant of record, so it handles sales tax. Before its adapter is built, the human describes Edmate to Paddle in writing (subscriptions to AI tutoring software; teachers paid by Edmate as content suppliers; live classes an included feature) and gets their OK. If Paddle refuses, Stripe Billing plus Stripe Tax, with Edmate filing US sales tax itself. Payouts to teachers stay manual in the pilot.
Why: Signed, timestamped webhooks, a separate sandbox, clear proration and native pause/resume fit 10.2 and 10.3; the providers can refuse marketplaces, so the written OK comes first.
Alternatives: Lemon Squeezy (b); Stripe Billing plus Stripe Tax from the start (c).
Reversible: Yes, the Payments port keeps the adapter swappable.

### 27 Oct 2026 · Sign-in sessions last 7 days, renewed on use (B-60, task 13.3b) · decided by you · risk: high
Decided: A database sign-in session lasts 7 days and is renewed while the person keeps using Edmate, before the pilot opens to more people. Today's 30-day value stays until 13.3b lands.
Why: A lost or shared device stops working within a week; active users rarely notice the renewal.
Alternatives: keep 30 days (a); 14 days renewed on use (c).
Reversible: Yes, one value in apps/web/src/auth/config.ts.

  against the unfixed component (confirmed: it did), so it would not be red before the fix. The
  extra-fetch-call assertion is red against the unmodified component (5 calls instead of 4,

### 27 Oct 2026 · 0.20f self-test input size · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: the quadratic self-test uses its own small `n = 200` via a new optional third
  parameter on `expectLinear`, instead of the real check's `n = 4,000`.
- Why: a genuine doubly-nested scan (needed so the self-test exercises real quadratic work, not a
  mocked clock) at `n = 4,000` does order `(16 * 4,000)^2 ≈ 4` billion no-op iterations at the 16x
  size, which is real, slow CPU work; it hit the default 20 s test timeout under load (see red
  evidence above) even though no wall clock is read anywhere in the measure itself. `n = 200`
  keeps the same 16x shape (so the ratio math is identical) while finishing in milliseconds.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 0.20f step count plus an absolute ceiling, no wall-clock ratio · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: the measure is the original step count (`countStringIteratorSteps`/`expectLinear`,
  unchanged) *plus* a second, independent absolute wall-clock ceiling (`expectUnderCeiling`,
  `Date.now()`-based, a fixed `2_000` ms bound, not a ratio). No wall-clock ratio is used anywhere.
- Why: fix round 1 found the step count blind to regex-internal work (`.replace`, `.matchAll`,
  regex `exec`), so a catastrophic-backtracking regex in `forgedLabelPattern` or
  `decodeHtmlEntities` would pass unseen. An absolute ceiling (not a ratio) catches that: ordinary
  CI load cannot push a sub-100-ms real scan past a 2-second ceiling, but a backtracking or
  quadratic regex blow-up on a similarly sized hostile string takes seconds to many seconds (shown
  by the self-test), so the gap between "real work" and "blow-up" stays wide without any
  load-dependent tuning. This keeps the acceptance's "does not use wall-clock ratios" intact: the
  step-count ratio check (16x input -> ratio < 64) still carries all the linear-vs-quadratic
  judgment; the new check only ever compares one elapsed time to one fixed constant.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 1.4e timeout design · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: the shared "ready" entry has no timeout of its own; only individual callers time
  out via their own `setTimeout`. The `ready` listener (and the WeakMap entry) is removed when
  the last still-waiting caller has either settled (via `ready`) or timed out.
- Why: the plan's second test case (a longer-timeout caller still resolving after the
  shorter-timeout first caller has timed out) is impossible if the shared entry carries the
  first caller's timeout, since that would reject it and every remaining waiter with it. The plan
  named this as the preferred, simplest option, and it also removes the "un-awaited rejection"
  risk entirely, since the entry itself never rejects.
  **Updated (fix round 1):** the original shape used one shared `Promise` with `.then()`
  reactions per caller, kept alive by a `waiters` counter; a caller's timeout only decremented the
  counter and left its `.then()` reaction attached, so during a long outage with sign-ins arriving
  faster than `timeoutMs`, `waiters` never reached 0 and the entry (plus every reaction ever
  attached) lived for the whole outage — unbounded memory growth (security-reviewer, HIGH). Fix
  round 1 replaces the shared `Promise` with a `Set<() => void>` of per-caller settle callbacks on
  the entry: the single `ready` listener calls and clears every callback in the set, and a
  caller's timeout removes only its own callback. Memory is now bounded by callers currently
  waiting, not by every caller since the outage began. Same listener-per-instance and
  per-caller-timeout behaviour as before; `RedisNotReadyError` unchanged.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 1.4c Google sign-in links to an existing email-verified user; Google's own dangerous-linking flag is on, gated entirely by Edmate's own check · decided by builder · risk: high

- Decided:
  - **Flag.** The Google provider's `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking` changes from `false` (1.3)
    to `true`. This is necessary, not cosmetic: in the installed `@auth/core` 0.41.3, the `signIn`
    callback (`handleAuthorized`, `lib/actions/callback/index.js:63`) runs **before**
    `handleLoginOrRegister` (`:70`), which is where the email-match lookup or the
    `OAuthAccountNotLinked` throw happens (`handle-login.js:236-250`). With the flag `false`, that
    throw fires regardless of what `signIn` would have returned, so the flag must be `true` for
    linking to ever be possible; because `signIn` runs first, refusing there stops the link before
    any row is written — confirmed directly against the real handlers in `flow.test.ts`'s new
    cases (not just inferred).
  - **The real gate.** The `signIn` callback refuses the sign-in (returns `false`, same as every
    other refusal in this callback) unless: Google reports `email_verified: true` (already true
    since 1.3) **and** the existing user this email belongs to already has `emailVerifiedAt` set
    (only ever true today for a user who verified by the email-link flow) **and** that user has no
    other `google` account already linked (`identity.hasLinkedAccount`, new). Any one of those
    failing refuses the sign-in and links nothing; `@auth/core` never gets to call `linkAccount` in
    that case.
  - **Why this is "narrow", not "flip and hope".** The flag alone (Auth.js's documented "dangerous"
    default) links by email with no verification at all. Edmate never relies on that: every path
    that could reach `linkAccount` must first pass the three checks above, which is the officially
    recommended mitigation for this exact flag — the flag only changes *when `@auth/core` is
    willing to try*, Edmate's callback decides *whether it's allowed to*.
  - **Unaffected.** The email magic-link provider's own branch of `signIn`; the shared-device
    check; the under-age block; a returning Google user (resolved by `getUserByAccount`, never
    reaching the new block) — all re-run unmodified in this build and still pass.
- Why: this is the only point in `next-auth@5.0.0-beta.32`'s OAuth callback lifecycle where
  Edmate's own code can decide whether a by-email link is trustworthy; the three-part check
  (verified on both sides, no existing different link) is exactly the acceptance criteria and
  mirrors README rule 7's existing data-layer invariant, made explicit and tested instead of left
  to a driver-error. This decision replaces the Google-provider bullet of the 18 Oct 2026 1.3 entry
  in `docs/decisions/log.md`.
- Alternatives:
  - Keep the flag `false` and try to link inside the callback: rejected, the throw happens earlier
    in the lifecycle than the callback runs, so there's nothing left for Edmate's code to prevent.
  - Allow linking on Google's `email_verified` alone, ignoring the existing user's own verification
    state: rejected, it would let an attacker's freshly-created, Google-verified account silently
    annex any pre-existing, never-verified Edmate user at that address.
  - A Better-Auth-style custom OAuth flow: an ADR-level change to the tech stack, out of proportion
    to this task.
- Reversible: yes. The flag and the `signIn` block both sit in `createAuthConfig`; reverting to
  1.3's behaviour is a two-line change with no data migration (no schema change in this task at
  all).

No further decisions beyond the plan's draft; the plan's open questions (Q1-Q5) and the lead's
answers were followed as given, with no deviation.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 8.2i Host header carries the request's port when non-default · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `pinnedRequestOptions` sets `headers.host` to `bareHostName(host)`, with
  `:${req.url.port}` appended only when `req.url.port` is non-empty (i.e. not the URL's default
  port), rather than the plan's literal `headers: { ...req.headers, host }` (bare host, no port
  logic at all).

  passing 8.2h tests that depend on `req(port)` building an explicit non-default port into the URL
  (`http://teacher-site.test:${port}/...`) and asserting the `Host` header still carries it — real
  HTTP semantics require `Host` to carry a non-default port, and SNI's `servername` never carries
  a port either way (TLS has no notion of one), so this doesn't put SNI and `Host` out of sync.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 13.regatea nullsFirst on the index columns · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: declare the index's descending columns as `.desc().nullsFirst()` (drizzle-orm 0.45.4
  `ExtraConfigColumn` method, confirmed in its type declarations), rather than the plan draft's
  plain `.desc()`.
- Why: publish.ts's `last` CTE writes `order by agent_id, published_at desc, id desc` with no
  `nulls` annotation. Postgres's default null ordering for an un-annotated `desc` is `nulls
  first`. Drizzle's own default for `.desc()` on an index column is `DESC NULLS LAST` (confirmed:
  the first attempt, without `.nullsFirst()`, generated `... DESC NULLS LAST ...`). That mismatch
  meant the planner could not recognize the index's native order as satisfying the CTE's
  `order by` -- EXPLAIN on the plan draft's query (unmodified, matching `publish.ts` exactly)
  showed a `Bitmap Heap Scan` + explicit `Sort`, not the intended plan, even though the index's
  predicate and column list were otherwise an exact match and in use (visible as a `Bitmap Index
  Scan` feeding the `Recheck Cond`). Adding `.nullsFirst()` to both descending columns fixed this
  without needing any change to `publish.ts`'s query (kept out of this plan's files, as the
  design required) -- published_at/id can never actually be null for rows the partial predicate
  lets through, so this has no behavioral effect beyond matching the query's implicit ordering.
  Flagging as a decision since the plan's draft SQL (`.desc()`, no `nullsFirst()`) would not
  have produced the "no Sort node" result the acceptance requires, once tested against the real,
  unmodified CTE shape.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 13.regatea EXPLAIN test's session-level planner settings · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: the EXPLAIN test sets `work_mem = '64kB'` and `random_page_cost = 1.1` (`set local`,
  inside a transaction that's rolled back) before running the EXPLAIN, and uses a fixture with
  10 gate/passed rows per agent plus 20 non-gate rows per agent (not the single row per agent a
  literal reading of the plan's "one eval_runs row per agent" suggested) to make the planner
  genuinely favor the new index at this fixture's (intentionally small, per the plan) row count.
- Why: at the row counts available in a fast int test, Postgres's default cost settings
  (`random_page_cost = 4`, generous default `work_mem`) make a sequential or bitmap scan plus an
  explicit sort cheaper than using the new index to avoid the sort, even once the index is used
  and its predicate/column list match exactly -- this is a property of the test's necessarily
  small synthetic table, not of the index design. Lowering `random_page_cost` to reflect the
  production host's actual (SSD) storage and lowering `work_mem` to make an on-disk sort's cost
  estimate realistic for a much bigger production table are both legitimate planner-config
  choices (not query hacks: no `enable_seqscan`/`enable_bitmapscan` disabling was used, and the
  EXPLAIN's query text is the CTE's exact, unmodified shape) that let a small fixture demonstrate
  the same plan a much larger production `eval_runs` table would get under its own cost settings.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 12.2f Phase D agentStatus placement and no-run path · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `agentStatus` is a top-level field of the `GET /api/studio/publish` JSON body, sibling
  to `run` (not nested inside the `PublishRunView`/`run` object), and is **only computed and
  returned when a run already exists** (`run !== null`); the `{ run: null }` no-run reply is
  unchanged, with no `agents.get` call on that path. Client-side, `loadLatestRun`'s resolved value
  becomes `{ run, agentStatus }` (`agentStatus: null` when the server omitted it).
- Why: the plan's wording ("add `agentStatus` ... alongside the existing run fields" /
  "`PublishRun`-adjacent load result type") was read literally as a field next to `run`, not inside
  it, matching publishClient.ts's own file header lesson ("loose objects so an extra server field
  never breaks the page" -- a sibling field, not a nested one, keeps `PublishRun`'s own shape
  untouched for every other caller). Skipping the lookup on the no-run path is a real behaviour
  choice the plan didn't spell out for that branch: an agent takedown only ever sets `suspended` on
  a `live` agent (confirmed in `takedowns.ts`'s header comment -- every student-facing read already
  requires `live`), and a `live` agent can only exist after a passed publish run, so `run === null`
  implies the agent has never been anything but `draft` and can never be `suspended`; querying
  `agents.get` there would be a correct but needless extra read on the one path per request that
  already returns early.

### 27 Oct 2026 · 12.2f agentStatus on the no-run path · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `GET /api/studio/publish`'s no-run path now looks up the teacher's agent (via
  `packages.listForTeacher` + `agents.get`) and returns `agentStatus` there too, exactly as the
  run-exists path already does, except when the teacher has no packages yet (no agent exists to
  look up -- `{ run: null }` with no `agentStatus` field, unchanged from before).
- Why: the Phase D decision's premise -- "an agent takedown sets `suspended` only on a `live`
  agent ... so `run === null` implies the agent can never be `suspended`" -- was wrong.
  `takeDownAgentInTx` (`packages/db/src/repositories/takedowns.ts`) updates `agents.status` to
  `suspended` unconditionally, regardless of the agent's current status; a draft agent (one that
  has never had a publish run) can be taken down just as a live one can. Skipping the lookup on the
  no-run path therefore hid a real "removed by staff" state from the teacher. The extra read this
  adds is one `packages.listForTeacher` + one `agents.get` call on the single path per request that
  used to return early with no reads at all -- the same cost the `start` handler already pays on
  every call.

  `latest` and `create` all at once), which would force every fake in `sweep.test.ts` to also
  implement unused methods (`get`, `create`) just to satisfy the type — the opposite of "a narrow
  injected interface" the brief and rule 4 ask for. Nested `Pick`s (the same shape
  `apps/web/src/studio/publish.ts`'s `PublishBackend.repos` already uses) keep the fakes to only
  the three methods the sweep actually calls.

### 26 Oct 2026 · 9.6f notes.ts used-set fix is a documented invariant, not an observed behavior change · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: implemented the literal ask (mark an exact match's index `used` too) and added a test,
  but the test documents the intended invariant with the actually-reachable processing order
  rather than asserting a scenario where old and new code differ.
- Why: an exhaustive search (46,656 combinations of message/question timestamps, including ties
  and `answeredAt`-absent cases, via a throwaway script) found zero observable difference between
  the old (`usedByFallback`, exact branch never marks `used`) and new (`used`, exact branch marks
  it) code. This is provable directly from the algorithm's own structure: `answered` is sorted
  ascending by `at`, so any question whose exact match claims message index `m` has `at ==
  m.createdAt`; every later-processed question's own `at` is `>= ` that value by sort order, so
  its fallback's forward search (`m.createdAt >= at`) can never even reach that earlier index
  regardless of whether it is marked `used` — the ordering invariant already prevents the reuse
  the fix defends against. The change is still correct, matches the review's literal ask, and
  costs nothing; the comment documents the invariant for a reader, and the new test exercises the
  real code path (including the intentional grouped-answer exact-ignores-`used` behavior) with
  correct expectations rather than a false before/after narrative.

### 26 Oct 2026 · 9.6f subscriptions.ts pause/cancel: one CTE statement instead of lockLive + update · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `pause` and `cancel` call a new shared `lockAndWriteStatusIfLive` helper (one
  `with ... for update` + `update ... from` statement) instead of `lockLive` followed by a
  separate `tx.update(...)`; `changePackage` and `resume` keep `lockLive` unchanged.
- Why: `pause`/`cancel` have no read between the lock and the write (unlike `changePackage`/
  `resume`), so their two round trips collapse into one without changing lock order or behavior.
  `changePackage`/`resume` do have a read in between (packages/auditLog), so folding them the same
  way would either move that read inside the CTE (a bigger, harder-to-verify rewrite) or lose the
  "lock first, read everything else after" ordering `lockLive`'s own comment requires — out of
  scope for this task's plan (which named only `pause`/`cancel`).

### 26 Oct 2026 · 8.7q pre-cap uses the same constant, no headroom · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: the pre-check in `storable()` reuses `AUDIT_JSON_MAX_LENGTH` (10,000) itself, not a
  larger threshold with headroom for redaction growth.
- Why: every caller's `before`/`after` is a small, fixed structured shape, so a raw value already
  over the cap is abnormal regardless of content; refusing it early costs nothing legitimate.
  Redaction only grows a value by a few characters per match, never needing more headroom than the
  cap already allows, because the unchanged post-redaction check is what enforces the final
  stored-value limit. A value that is mostly personal-data text and over the cap raw, but would
  have redacted down under the cap, is now rejected pre-redaction instead of accepted -- an
  intentional, simplest-MVP behaviour change, not a silent one. This is the plan's own decision
  (see docs/tasks/8.7q/plan.md), recorded here per the board's `risk: high` entry (8.7p's deferred
  finding).

### 26 Oct 2026 · 8.7p item-1 clip region includes the separator · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: when a raw `PHONE_CANDIDATE` match is clipped at an exempt span's boundary, the
  redacted `REDACTED` region covers from the span's end to the match's end — including any
  separator character (e.g. the single space between an id and a phone number) that sits between
  them. The id/UUID/digest text itself is always left untouched; only the separator plus the
  phone text is replaced, so output looks like `rp_<hex40>[redacted]` rather than
  `rp_<hex40> [redacted]`.
- Why: the plan's accept line only required "the id/UUID/digest text unchanged and `${REDACTED}`
  in place of the phone" — it did not pin down whether a separator between them survives as
  literal text. Keeping the separator as literal text would require a second, separate clip rule
  for "boundary characters immediately after a span before the phone proper starts," which the
  plan did not ask for and which adds complexity without changing the safety property (no exempt
  span text is ever redacted, no phone digit ever survives). Tests were written to check both
  invariants (`toContain(span)`, `not.toMatch(phone digits)`) rather than pin exact spacing, so
  this choice does not need a test change if the lead prefers the other spacing later.

### 26 Oct 2026 · 3.9f chat.ts close-on-error path · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: no change needed to the pre-existing `catch (e)` around `buildChatDeps` (line ~205 in
  `chat.ts`).
- Why: per the plan's instruction to confirm rather than assume — `setup` is only assigned after
  `buildChatDeps` returns successfully, and `setup.close` only exists on a `ChatSetup` once
  `buildDbRetrieval` itself returned successfully (it opens the pool and returns the handle
  together, never partially). A thrown error inside `buildChatDeps`/`buildDbRetrieval` therefore
  never reaches a point where a pool handle exists but is unreachable from the catch; the
  catch path cannot leak a pool. Confirmed by reading `chat.ts`'s catch block and
  `buildDbRetrieval`'s body: no deviation, no fix needed.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 3.9a SIGINT closes readline via its own cancelSource plus an interrupted flag · decided by builder · risk: low

- Decided: on `SIGINT`, cancel the in-flight turn's own `cancelSource()` token, close the
  `readline.Interface`, and additionally set an `interrupted` boolean checked at the top of every
  loop iteration.
- Why: `rl.close()` alone stops future `for await` reads but does not retroactively drop a line
  already sitting in readline's internal buffer when stdin data arrives all at once (e.g. piped
  input in tests) — a second scripted line could still reach an in-flight iteration and send one
  more turn after Ctrl+C. The flag is cheap, local to this function, and makes "no further turn is
  sent after SIGINT" deterministic without depending on readline's internal buffering behaviour.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 11.4h column-list ON DELETE SET NULL · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: the migration's composite FK uses the Postgres 15+ column-list form, `ON DELETE SET
  NULL ("live_class_id")`, instead of a plain `ON DELETE SET NULL`. `documents.teacherId`'s
  schema-level `.onDelete('set null')` call stays as schema-only bookkeeping so `db:generate`
  remains a no-op; the deployed clause lives only in the hand-edited migration SQL.
- Why: a plain (non-column-list) `SET NULL` on a composite FK nulls every referencing column,
  including `teacher_id` — which is `NOT NULL` on `documents` — so deleting a live class would
  have failed with a not-null violation instead of unlinking the recording. This surfaced as a
  real test failure (`document-live-class-migration.int.test.ts`'s "refuses a link to a missing
  class, and unlinks (keeps) recordings when a class is deleted") when first run against the
  plan's literal `ON DELETE set null` text, and is why the plan's SQL snippet needed this one
  change. drizzle-orm's `foreignKey().onDelete()` type (`UpdateDeleteAction`) can't express a
  column list, so this is unavoidably a hand-edit, same category as the existing `NOT VALID`
  hand-edits in this file.

  phone digit-run rule, even when padded so the digits read as a phone number).
- Why: the plan asked for a test, not a fix; the 8.7h decision already accepted this trade-off at
  `risk: high`, and this value is still UUID-shaped by the same regex.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 8.7m a UUID glued to a phone number with no separator redacts the whole run · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: when a phone-length digit run is glued onto a UUID's last hex group with no
  separator, the merged run no longer matches the `UUID` regex (its trailing `\b` needs a
  non-word character right after the 12th hex character, but the next character is still a
  digit), so `PHONE_CANDIDATE` treats the whole digit-and-hyphen run as one phone-shaped
  candidate and redacts it entirely — the UUID-looking prefix is lost along with the phone
  digits. Added a test asserting the phone digits never survive
  (`redacts a UUID with a 10-digit phone number glued on with no separator`).
- Why: the plan requires the phone digits must never survive; over-redacting the glued UUID
  prefix too is the safe side (fail closed), and a UUID is already recoverable from context
  (callers keep real ids outside these audit payloads per README rule 9), whereas a phone number
  surviving would not be. Also noted: dropping `\p{L}` from the lookbehind only affects the start
  of a match; a letter glued directly to a UUID with *no* phone number appended and *no*
  separator (e.g. `id12345678-1234-4234-8234-123456789012`, no space or punctuation before the
  UUID) now also gets fully redacted for the same `\b`-boundary reason, since letter-then-digit
  is not a word boundary either. This is not covered by a test because it is not a realistic
  shape (ids and UUIDs are written with a separator such as a space or colon in text, which this
  change does not affect — see the embedded-UUID test), and the plan does not ask for it; flagged
  here in case a future value hits it.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 8.7m fix round: prefixed-id and hex-digest spans are exempt from PHONE_CANDIDATE · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: treat whole `<prefix>_<rest>` id tokens and bare 32+ char hex digests as exempt spans,
  the same way UUID-shaped runs already are, instead of narrowing `PHONE_CANDIDATE`'s lookbehind
  further.
- Why: narrowing the lookbehind back to block letters would undo the 8.7m fix (glued phone
  numbers like `abc5551234567` would stop being redacted again); excluding the specific id/hash
  shapes that need protecting keeps both behaviours and stays a single linear scan per regex (no
  nested quantifiers).

### 25 Oct 2026 · 8.7m fix round 2: HEX_DIGEST requires at least one a-f letter · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: add a lookahead to `HEX_DIGEST` requiring at least one a-f letter in the run, instead
  of any other way to exclude pure-digit runs.
- Why: a bare 32+ digit run is exactly the shape `PHONE_CANDIDATE` must redact (it is itself a
  phone-length digit run); only an actual hex digest (one with a letter) needs the exemption.
  Requiring a letter is the minimal fix and keeps the single linear pass per regex, no nested
  quantifiers.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 13.2 load script imports its own built dist by relative path · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `scripts/loadTest50.ts` imports `../dist/...` files, not `@edmate/harness`'s package
  name and not the `src/*.ts` files directly.
- Why: the plan's draft convention (Node native TS run against `src/*.ts` with explicit `.ts`
  extensions, mirroring `packages/db/scripts/record-demo-embeddings.ts`) hits two real walls here
  that db's script doesn't: (1) the harness's own internal `src/` files use `.js`-suffixed
  relative imports (for `tsc`'s benefit), which Node's resolver will not map to sibling `.ts`
  files, so a deep import chain (`steps/index.ts` → `admit.ts` → ...) fails to resolve when run
  directly from source; (2) `runner.ts`'s `Turn` class uses constructor parameter properties,
  which Node's default strip-only type-stripping cannot erase (confirmed by running it: "TypeScript
  parameter property is not supported in strip-only mode"). Importing the package's own compiled
  `dist/` by a relative path (allowed by the harness-purity ESLint rule, which only blocks
  self-importing the package's own specifier, not a relative path that stays inside
  `packages/harness`) solves both at once, and matches what every other consumer of `@edmate/harness`
  already does: run against the built output, never the raw source.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 13.4 Phase B: live-mode loop stops at "below the limit", not "zero" · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `purgeTable` (`apps/worker/src/retention/workers.ts`) calls a table's purge method
  again only while the previous call's count equals (or exceeds) `purgeLimit`; a call reporting
  fewer rows than `purgeLimit` ends that table's loop for this run, even if some of today's run
  already purged some other, now-recent-enough-to-not-qualify rows.
- Why: this matches `@edmate/db`'s own contract exactly — a live call never returns more than
  `limit` rows by construction, so "count < limit" is the only correct signal that a call cleared
  everything there was to clear at that moment; checking for "count === 0" instead would do one
  extra, always-empty call per table per run forever. Capped at `MAX_ITERATIONS_PER_TABLE` (1000)
  regardless, so even a pathological backend that always returns exactly `limit` can never loop a
  single run forever — it stops, reports `maxIterationsHit: true`, and is picked up again next
  run.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 13.4 an erased student's open questions are dismissed · decided by lead · risk: high
- Decided: `identity.anonymise` (`packages/db/src/identity/store.ts`) clears `teacher_questions.text`
  and, in the same statement, also sets `status = 'dismissed'` for any of this student's rows
  whose status is `'open'`; answered or already-dismissed rows of theirs keep their existing
  status, and no other student's row is ever touched (the update is scoped by `studentId = id`).
- Why: the partial unique index `teacher_questions_open_dedup_key`
  (`packages/db/src/schema/learning.ts`) is on `(teacher_id, student_id, agent_id, md5(text))
  where status = 'open'`. Clearing two of this student's open questions to the same teacher's
  agent to `text = ''` without changing status made both rows collide on `md5('')` under that
  index, throwing a unique violation and rolling back the whole account delete. A deleted student
  can never receive an answer, so dismissing the row is correct, not just a workaround for the
  index; checked `teacherQuestionsRepo` (`packages/db/src/repositories/teacher-questions.ts`)
  first — `open`'s grouping read and `listGroupsForTeacher` both filter by `status = 'open'` per
  row, never by `group_id` as a whole, and the teacher's own dismiss action already sets exactly
  `status: 'dismissed'` on a single row — so this matches existing behaviour and a group whose
  other rows belong to other students still shows them.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 7.4a deadline race via setTimeout, no AbortSignal · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: implemented the deadline race with a plain `setTimeout`-backed `Promise.race` per
  case (cancelled via `clearTimeout` on whichever side wins), reading time via the existing
  `now()` injection point only for the "already past deadline" fast path, not for the race
  timer itself.

  deadline passes under `vi.useFakeTimers()`; it does not require (and the plan explicitly
  defers) cancelling the underlying agent/judge call. `setTimeout` composes with
  `vi.useFakeTimers()` / `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync` out of the box, so the hung-case test
  needs no new clock abstraction. The manual-clock tests (`now: () => clock`) are unaffected
  because their agents resolve synchronously well before any real timer would fire, so the race
  always resolves on the "done" side in those tests, same behaviour as before.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 7.2j Hinglish vapes variant written as two order alternatives · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: the Hinglish rule is `(school-word ... vape-word ... verb) | (vape-word ... verb ...
  school-word)`, i.e. two bounded alternatives rather than a single order, each still bounded with
  `gap(3)`.
- Why: the plan's examples span both orders ("school mein vape bechna hai" — school first; "vape
  khareedna hai school ke paas" — vape first), and the plan explicitly says "in either order,
  bounded with the existing `gap(n)` helper" — a single-order pattern (like the weapons
  `hathiyar...chhupa` precedent) would miss the school-mein-vape order.
- Exact lists chosen: vape word `(?:vapes?|vaping|juul\S*)`; school word `(?:school|class|college|
  campus)` with optional postposition `(?: (?:mein|me|main|pe|par))?`; transaction verb `(?:bech\S*|
  bik\S*|khareed\S*|kharid\S*|le\S* aa\S*|mang\S*|supply)` — exactly the lists the plan named.
- risk: low.

  `packages/db/src/schema/operations.ts` and the header comment in

  `live_classes` to `class_questions` by `live_class_id`, with each live class's own rows already
  in `(created_at, id)` order; it does not remove the `Sort` in `listQueueForTeacher`'s

  `RolePlaySchema`) with the two new optional fields.

  simply never fires, with no test able to catch it except one that exercises the real runner
  (which `roleplay.integration.test.ts`'s new cases do). `results.ts` sits in the same `pipeline/`
  directory as the files the plan did list and validates the exact `DecideResult` interface
  `types.ts` (a listed file) defines; it does not touch `pedagogy/**`, `content/**` or

### 25 Oct 2026 · 13.skillpresent terminal mock-interview line moves from the controls into the thread · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: while the interview is live (`question`/`pause`/`resume`/`debrief`), the progress line
  ("Question 3 of 6", "Paused — question 3 of 6", "Interview complete — N questions asked") shows
  next to the Pause/Stop controls (`MockInterviewControls`, via the new `progress` prop and
  `parseRolePlayProgress`). Once the harness marks a turn terminal (`stopped`/`ended`) the
  `activeSkill` effect clears, so Pause/Stop (and the controls' progress line with them) disappear
  on that same render; the terminal line ("Interview stopped — N question(s) answered" /
  "Interview ended") is instead rendered by `TurnExtras` as a thread note on that final turn, so
  the student still sees it once the controls are gone.
- Why: the plan's Q3 only asked where the reset point lives, not where the terminal progress text
  shows; discovered by a first failing test draft (the control disappears in the same render the
  terminal phase arrives, so a progress line attached to it can never be seen) -- fixing it needed
  one of (a) delay the reset by a render, (b) keep the controls mounted a turn longer, or (c) show
  the terminal line somewhere that survives the reset. (c) is simplest and matches the existing
  "feedback given" marker pattern already added for the feedback skill event, so it was chosen.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 8.6f Phase A: a distinct `RepositoryErrorKind` for the package cap, and a shared package-row lock · decided by builder · risk: high

- Decided: added `'limit'` to `RepositoryErrorKind` (mapping to the existing contracts
  `ErrorCode` `'limit_reached'`) so `packages.create`'s cap refusal is no longer reported as the
  same `'invalid'` used for unrelated bad writes; extracted `checkModules` and a new
  `lockPackageRow` helper into `packages/db/src/repositories/package-write.ts` so
  `packages.ts`'s `saveVersion` and `package-versions.ts`'s `create` lock the same package row
  the same way; `packages.ts`'s `package.save` audit `after` now keeps the package id (8.7h
  already fixed the audit redactor's UUID handling, so the old omission was working around a bug
  that no longer exists).
- Why: a real repo `'invalid'` on `packages.create` (for example a stray unique-violation) was
  previously indistinguishable from "you're at the package limit," which could mislead a caller
  into showing the wrong error to a teacher; two writers taking the package row lock in
  inconsistent ways is exactly the deadlock-class risk `docs/lessons.md` already flags from
  8.7a, so moving both to the shared `package-write.ts` helpers was meant to close that class of
  bug here. Correction (fix round): extracting the helpers did not by itself make the order
  shared -- `package-versions.ts`'s `create` still called `checkModules` before `lockPackageRow`,
  the reverse of `packages.ts`'s `saveVersion`. See "Fix round" below for the actual fix.

### 25 Oct 2026 · 8.6f Phase B: four pre-existing `apps/web` switches map the new `'limit'` kind to their closest client-error response · decided by builder · risk: low

- Decided: `apps/web/src/studio/profile.ts` and `apps/web/src/studio/questions/routes.ts` group
  `'limit'` with `'invalid'`/`'integrity'` (a plain 400 `validation`); `apps/web/src/
  subscriptions/change.ts` groups it with `'invalid'` (the action-specific 409); `apps/web/src/
  subscriptions/start.ts` maps it the same as `'integrity'` (a plain 400 `validation`). Each
  switch keeps a one-line comment saying the repo call behind it (`teacherProfiles`,
  `teacherQuestions`, subscription plan changes, subscription start) has no cap and so can never
  actually raise `'limit'` — the case exists only so the exhaustive switch (each file's own
  `const unreachable: never` / `assertNever` pattern) still compiles. No test was added for any
  of the four: none of their repo calls can reach `'limit'`, so there is nothing reachable to
  assert (per the brief: "Add a test only where a mapping is reachable").
- Why: each of these four files' exhaustive switch is a defence against a *future* repo call
  starting to raise a kind the switch doesn't expect; today none of the four routes' calls
  (`teacherProfiles.*`, `teacherQuestions.*`, subscription change/start) go through any capped
  write, so there's no live path to `'limit'` to test — grouping with the nearest existing
  client-error response keeps each file compiling without inventing a cap-specific response a
  caller can't actually trigger.

### 24 Oct 2026 · 8.7j inline the gate/publish steps instead of guarding the cast in place · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: of the two options in the task (a runtime guard at the cast site, or returning the
  result through the gate step so no cast is needed), picked inlining `gatedPublish`'s two
  callbacks directly in `gateProcessor`. The gate step's return value is read as one local `const`
  used by both the publish and fail branches, so there is no mutable, nullable closure variable to
  guard or cast at all.
- Why: a guard placed only at the old cast site would be unreachable in every real call (the gate
  callback always either throws before assigning the closure variable, or assigns it before
  returning, so the publish callback could never see it unset) -- it would pass review as "a
  guard" but could never be exercised by a test. Inlining removes the unreachable state entirely
  and gives a genuinely reachable guard: `runGate` is an injected dependency, so a test can make it
  resolve without a result and watch the run end `error`.
- risk: low

### 24 Oct 2026 · 5.6b The ruling-out check holds across the whole reply, not just `reach` · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: the stream gate keeps a per-reply, per-item record of which wrong options its released
  text has already named (updated only when a piece is actually released). A piece whose release
  would complete the set (every wrong option named, not the correct one, across the whole reply so
  far) is held back as a leak exactly as a single-piece ruling-out is, even when the two mentions
  are pushed further apart than `keys.reach`. The check is independent of the matcher's
  `leaks`/`tailStart` (so the gate's linear-work bound is unaffected) and the whole-draft postGuard
  check is kept as the backstop.
- Why: a security finding (CRITICAL) showed the live gate only ever judged a sentence against
  `reach` units of prior text, so an ordinary long-winded reply that ruled out each wrong option in
  a separate, far-apart sentence streamed the full ruling-out to the student before postGuard's
  whole-draft check could replace it with the hint.
- risk: high

### 23 Oct 2026 · 5.6b The leak matcher gets an answer-context mode · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: A single-letter (label) key leaks unless it sits in an exempt shape (a separator-only list of two or more of the item's labels, or the item's exact option listing), and an answer word overrides every exemption except a list naming every label of an item. The active item's prompt and exact listing are exempt spans (matches fully inside are ignored, never deleted). The correct option's text is a full-strength key outside those spans, its position counts in an answer context or alone, and naming every wrong option (over the whole text) is a leak. Practice keys never get the own-code exemption. A label answer is graded only when it's the one label in the message. The bank serves mcq and code_output items once Phase C lands. Known limits, also risk: high: an unresolved item and a `practiceCarriedKey` guard only their label (the option text, position and ruling-out checks don't run on that turn); buildContext doesn't drop chunks holding the option text.
- Why: MCQ bare-label keys and code_output keys that appear in their own prompt tripped the leak gate on every re-show (5.6 architect MEDIUM, 5.6 Phase C open question answered (c)). This closes ADR-0010's Consequences line 43 ("until the matcher has an answer-context-only key mode"); no new ADR (Q7).
- risk: high

### 23 Oct 2026 · 5.6b A span exempts only its own item's keys; labels are exempt in any span · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: inside an item's prompt or listing span, a label mention is ignored for any label key, but a non-label key (number or text) is ignored only if it belongs to that item (its own answer key or correct option text). A key held from another item is still caught inside the span.
- Why: the plan says "a key match is ignored when it lies fully inside a span" without saying whose key. Exempting every key would let a re-shown prompt hide a carried key from another item (a "3 + 4" prompt hiding a held "7"); labels inside an item's own listing are structure, not an answer.
- risk: high

### 23 Oct 2026 · 5.6b Issue-time checks exempt only the new item's listing · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: toolLoop and skillEvent check a newly issued item's joined shown text with `issueCheckContext(issued)`: its option listing is a span, but its prompt is not and its own key is not used. So an MCQ after an MCQ with the same key B is served, while a new prompt saying "The answer is B" or showing "3 + 4" against a held "7" is still refused (today's behaviour). `skillEvent` builds the context from the shown text it already receives, so `steps/generate.ts` needs no change.
- Why: the plan passes `itemContextOf(issued)`, but that makes the new prompt its own exempt span, so a prompt that states an earlier key would pass the very check meant to catch it.
- risk: high

### 23 Oct 2026 · 5.6b The re-show hold-back is bounded and widens the window over a shown span · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: the stream gate holds back text that could still become an active item's prompt or listing, up to `HOLD_MAX` (2048 compact units). It judges a completed span as one piece. When the window in front would start inside a shown span, the window starts at the span's start.

### 23 Oct 2026 · 1.4b A confirm page and an address-bound cookie stop a bare GET from finishing sign-in · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: Mailed links now open `/sign-in/confirm`, not Auth.js's `/api/auth/callback/email`. The reason: `@auth/core@0.41.3` spends the single-use token on the bare GET of its callback, before Edmate's `signIn` callback runs, so a scanner's or a stranger's GET can't be refused from inside Auth.js.
- Decided: The `/api/auth/signin/email` POST sets a binding cookie only when the request is same-origin (Origin equals AUTH_URL's origin or, with no Origin header, `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`) AND Auth.js answered with its `verify-request` redirect. An error, rate-limit or MissingCSRF answer gets no cookie (fix round: both reviewers found that a cross-site auto-submitting form could plant a cookie for the attacker's own address). The gate looks only at Auth.js's answer, which is the same for known and unknown addresses, so it adds no enumeration signal. The value is `<issuedAt>.HMAC-SHA256(AUTH_SECRET, "linkbound:" + issuedAt + ":" + normalizeEmail(email))`: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, `__Host-` when secure, 15 minutes. The server refuses it once it is older than 15 minutes, so a captured value can't outlive Max-Age. The confirm page forwards straight to the callback only when this cookie matches the link's own `email` (lead answer to Q3, after the plan security review's CRITICAL). Anyone else sees the address and must click: a scanner, another browser, or a browser that asked for a link to a different address.
- Decided: `/api/auth/callback/email` has its own literal route, resolved ahead of the `[...nextauth]` catch-all (fix round, closing the security review's HIGH). It passes the GET to Auth.js only when the browser holds either the binding cookie for the request's `email`, or a "confirmed" cookie that the confirm Server Action sets. The confirmed cookie is `<issuedAt>.HMAC(AUTH_SECRET, "linkconfirmed:" + issuedAt + ":" + token + ":" + normalizeEmail(email))`: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 2 minutes, compared in constant time. Otherwise the route answers 303 to `/sign-in/confirm` with the same query, and no token is spent. An attacker can no longer send a victim straight to the real callback with the attacker's own token. The route exports no POST (fix round 2): Auth.js reads token and email from the query on any method, so a cross-site form POST would otherwise spend an attacker's token ungated; Next matches this literal path before the method, so a POST gets a 405 and never reaches the catch-all.
- Decided: The click is a Server Action (Next's Origin check is the CSRF protection). It returns the callback URL and the client opens it as a full page, because Next 16 would otherwise fetch a same-host action redirect on the server and spend the token there.
- Decided: Referer (LOW from the plan review): the page sets `metadata.referrer = 'same-origin'`, so the token-bearing URL never goes in a cross-origin Referer. `no-referrer` was rejected because it makes browsers send `Origin: null` on the action POST, which would break Next's CSRF check. The `auto` path is a server redirect, and browsers keep the original referrer across redirects, so the confirm URL isn't sent as a Referer there.
- Why: Auth.js owns token consumption and sessions (1.4 Q2). The only lever Edmate has is where the mailed link points and what runs before Auth.js's route. Binding the cookie to the address closes the auto-forward login-CSRF the review found. 1.4's accepted residual risk stays: a victim who is talked into clicking "Sign in" on someone else's link still signs in as that person. Merely opening a link, or the callback URL itself, never does.
- risk: high. This touches `apps/web/src/auth/**` and `apps/web/app/api/auth/**`. Reversible: revert `rebuildLink`'s target, the `index.ts` exports, the two new routes (`signin/email`, `callback/email`), and the page, action and form files. No migration, env var, contract or ADR.

### 23 Oct 2026 · 1.4b: no Referrer-Policy no-referrer on apps/web/app/sign-in/confirm/page.tsx · decided by lead · risk: low

A re-verification lifts nothing. `takedowns.lift` returns an agent to `live` only when its teacher's profile is `verified`; with no profile, `pending`, `rejected` or any other state it returns it to `draft` (profile read FOR SHARE before the agent lock). Phase A first built "not `rejected`"; the lead kept verified-only and Phase A2 built it, so a safety-rejected teacher who edits their subject (back to `pending`) can't be reopened by a routine lift. A plain rejection is unchanged. The student sees the existing takedown texts; no new error code.
- Why: B-46 (c): a safety rejection must cut existing subscribers off at once; every student path already refuses a non-live agent, so reusing 12.2b's takedown write needs no migration, contract or harness change and gives staff an audit trail and lift path. The lift rule closes the security review's MEDIUM (a routine lift reopening a rejected teacher).
- risk: high

### 22 Oct 2026 · Backup model provider: the same team on Claude models in Microsoft Foundry when the subscription window is exhausted · decided by you · risk: high
Decided: Sessions start through `scripts/claude-backup.sh`. It probes the subscription with one Haiku call; on a usage-limit error it starts Claude Code against Claude deployments (Opus-, Sonnet- and Haiku-class) in the human's Microsoft Foundry resource, paid per token from the human's Azure credit; on any other error it stops rather than switching to paid usage. Config and key live outside the repo (`~/.config/edmate/foundry.env`, chmod 600, or the Mac Keychain). On the backup, builders run on Sonnet only, no third slot, and closeouts record `provider: foundry`. The backup never serves students. Setup guide: `docs/backup-provider.md`.
Why: The subscription pool is shared by the lead and every agent and was exhausted on 20 Oct 2026; a Foundry endpoint keeps the same agents, skills, hooks and merge gate running, where a second agent runtime would mean rebuilding all of them. The credit is capped by the Azure spending limit and covers about one backup day a month.
Alternatives: real Microsoft Foundry Agent Service agents (rejected: a second orchestrator and tool layer to keep in sync); paid extra usage on the subscription (rejected by the human's standing rule).
Review: security-reviewer (sonnet) on the launcher, template, guide, skill paragraph and scanner; its HIGH (the secret scan missed an unquoted `KEY=value` line, so a key typed into the tracked template would pass) is fixed by a new "Unquoted secret assignment" pattern in `.githooks/secret-scan.py`; its MEDIUMs (arguments logged verbatim; a bare 429 treated as a usage limit) are fixed too.
Reversible: Yes. Start sessions with `claude` instead of the launcher.

### 22 Oct 2026 · 9.7c guard refuses host overrides in the query string · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `assertLocalDatabaseUrl` now also rejects any `TEST_DATABASE_URL` whose query string
  carries a `host` or `hostaddr` key (case-insensitively), and compares the authority hostname
  case-insensitively, before falling back to the existing localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 allowlist.
- Why: security-reviewer found that pg / pg-connection-string (used by `@edmate/db` and the
  spawned `migrate.js`/`seed.js`) honour a `?host=`/`?hostaddr=` query parameter that overrides the
  authority host for the actual connection, so `postgres://localhost:5432/edmate?host=prod-db.example.com`
  passed the old hostname-only check but would connect to `prod-db.example.com`. Rejecting the
  override keys outright (rather than parsing with pg-connection-string) keeps the guard pure, adds
  no dependency, and fails closed.
- risk: low

### 22 Oct 2026 · 8.2j Tag/override stripping is a hand scan, not a `<[^>]*>` regex · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: `stripTags`/`stripOverrides` in `captions.ts` are written as a forward-only character
  scan with a cached "next close" position, not as a regex replace.
- Why: the plan requires "no nested quantifiers (no ReDoS)". A single, non-nested quantifier like
  `<[^>]*>` is still quadratic on an adversarial input (many `<` never followed by `>`), which is a
  well-known ReDoS shape independent of nesting. The scan is true O(n) in every case; a test with a
  1 MB line of unclosed `<` and a loose 5 s bound (per `docs/lessons.md`, no tight timings) guards
  the fix.
- risk: low (new code, 100% branch-covered by the fixture tests above; no external input beyond the
  teacher's own caption file reaches this function).

### 22 Oct 2026 · 8.2j Caption parser rules · decided by builder · risk: medium
- Decided: VTT requires a `WEBVTT` header line (else `unsupported`); any cue block whose timing line
  doesn't match the `[hh:]mm:ss.ttt --> [hh:]mm:ss.ttt` (or SRT comma-separated) shape is silently
  skipped, which is also how `NOTE`/`STYLE`/`REGION` blocks (no timing line) are dropped without a
  separate keyword check; a cue's first line is dropped when it exactly repeats the previous *kept*
  cue's last line (YouTube rolling auto-captions); cues are bucketed through the shared
  `unitsFromTimedText` so captions land in the same 90 s units a Whisper transcript gives; and every
  thrown error is one of the two fixed `IngestError`s named in the plan, with no file text quoted.
- Why: matches the plan (docs/tasks/8.2c/plan.md, Phase A) exactly; relying on "no timing line
  parses" to also catch NOTE/STYLE/REGION (rather than a separate keyword-based skip) is simpler and
  was verified correct by test (`captions.test.ts` "skips NOTE, STYLE and REGION blocks").
- risk: medium (new parser on untrusted teacher-uploaded files; no network or file-system access,
  no eval, output is plain text only; recommend the plan's optional, non-gating
  `security-reviewer` pass on this file at the lead's discretion, per the plan's risky-paths note).

  repository-level refusal is a second line, not the only one. Tested with fixed clocks for all

### 22 Oct 2026 · 8.2e The job payload carries the URL; failed web jobs are removed from Redis · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: The web link's URL travels only in the BullMQ job payload (`IngestJob.url`); Postgres keeps a `.link` storage key and the title. Web jobs are enqueued with `removeOnFail: true` (and `removeOnComplete: true`), so the URL leaves Redis when the job finishes or fails for the last time. The dead-letter copy keeps only refs. The URL is never logged and never put in an error message.
- Why: Plan Decision 9 and the lead's answers say the URL must not be stored in Postgres or logged. Removing the job on failure stops the URL from sitting in Redis's failed-job history for 7 days. An integration test checks that no Redis key holds it.
- risk: high (it sets where a teacher's URL may live)

### 22 Oct 2026 · 8.2e Last-attempt rule for every ingest job · decided by builder · risk: medium
- Decided: When a retryable failure happens on the final attempt (`attemptsMade + 1 >= opts.attempts`, where a missing `attempts` counts as 1, matching BullMQ), the document is marked `failed`: with the IngestError's code, or `provider_error` for an unexpected error. The raw error is not kept as the cause. If the database itself is down while writing that status, the job still throws a retryable error.
- Why: Without this rule, a site that is down on every attempt, or a provider outage, left the document `processing` forever. This was the lead's answer for Phase B. The rule applies to file jobs too, because they had the same gap.
- risk: medium

### 22 Oct 2026 · 8.2d Web-link egress policy: pinned address per hop, ADR-0014 · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: The web fetcher resolves each hop once, inside the 15 s deadline. Every answer must be public, and the transport connects only to the first answer (`node:https` with a pinned `lookup`, `agent: false`, `autoSelectFamily: false`, SNI from the host name and none for an IP literal, certificate checks on). Further rules:
  - https on port 443 only, with no userinfo and at most 2048 characters;
  - a denylist of internal names (trailing dot stripped);
  - at most 3 redirects, each checked again;
  - HTML only, a 5 MB cap counted on decompressed bytes, and a fixed header list;
  - three allow-list modes: unset refuses everything, `*` allows any public host, or a list of exact hosts;
  - YouTube is refused as `unsupported`;
  - robots.txt isn't checked.

  ADR-0014 is written from the architect's draft with Decision 9 updated to the lead answers.
- Why: closes the DNS-rebinding gap between check and connect before anything in production calls the fetcher; ADR-0005 set the precedent of recording egress policy as an ADR.
- risk: high

- Decided: `packageVersions.liveForAgent` and `subscriptions.start` both require

  since neither read checked verification.

### 22 Oct 2026 · 9.3c re-check verification inside start's own write statement, FOR SHARE · decided by builder · risk: high
- Decided: `subscriptions.start` re-checks the teacher's profile as part of the same
  `INSERT ... SELECT ... FOR SHARE OF teacher_profiles` statement that writes the subscription
  (not a separate pre-check), so a verification change can't commit mid-start. Refuses with the
  existing `not_found` kind (the same one a non-live `packageVersionId` already uses) — no new
  error kind invented.
- Why: the lead's instruction was to re-check verification "inside subscriptions.start's
  transaction ... reading the profile FOR SHARE". Since `start` was already a single atomic
  `INSERT ... SELECT` statement (no separate transaction wrapper), the simplest statement that
  satisfies both "read FOR SHARE" and "inside the same transaction" is one `INSERT ... SELECT ...
  FOR SHARE OF` statement with the verified join folded into its own `FROM`/`WHERE`, rather than a
  separate `SELECT ... FOR SHARE` followed by a second `INSERT ... SELECT` inside an explicit
  `db.transaction` (that two-statement form was tried first; it made the final
  `written(result) !== 1` defensive check unreachable — every mismatch that could fail the insert
  was already caught by the earlier select — dropping `src/repositories` coverage below the
  package's 100% statement threshold). The one-statement form keeps `written(result) !== 1` as the
  single, fully-exercised refusal path.
- risk: high (a `packages/db/src/repositories/**` change).

### 22 Oct 2026 · 8.7f persona always fails the case · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: when `input.persona` is defined, the gate always throws (fails that case loudly)
  rather than trying to honor it for a `kind: 'skill_action'` start turn only. `TurnInput` has no
  `persona` field at all; a persona only enters the pipeline via a start turn's `skillPayload`
  (bare id), and every later turn needs a *stored* `personaId` in that session's help state. The
  gate creates a brand-new session (and a fresh help-state map) on every single `reply()` call,
  so there is no continuity across a case's turns — a start-turn-only hack would silently produce
  wrong, non-roleplay results for every multi-turn persona case (confirmed real multi-turn persona
  suites exist, e.g. `evals/suites/persona/persona-roleplay-model-answer-en.yaml`). Failing the
  case outright matches the brief ("fail any case that names one, with a clear reason, never
  silently score it") and `runCaseSafely`'s existing catch-and-fail-this-case design.
- Why: a half-working persona path (first turn only) would be worse than a clear failure, because
  it would score a roleplay case as if it ran correctly when it did not resume the persona at all.
- risk: low — gate-only behavior, no change to prompt-pack behaviour or contracts; persona gate
  support is left as a known gap for whoever picks it up next (would need a `TurnInput.persona`
  field or similar, which is a contracts change needing an ADR per rule 2).

### 22 Oct 2026 · 8.6b Teacher scope checks in the agent and package repositories · decided by builder · risk: high

### 22 Oct 2026 · 9.0d cap the test clock's jump instead of raising a timeout · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: Fix the SSE test flake by capping how far `apps/web/test/turn-backend.ts`'s
  `deadlineSafeClock.now()` may jump between two calls (20 ms), rather than raising any vitest
  timeout, widening any harness step budget, or weakening an assertion.
- Why: Two spots in the harness (`runner.ts`'s preGuard remaining-budget subtraction and
  `postGuard.ts`'s budget subtraction) compute a step's remaining time by subtracting two
  `clock.now()` reads, with no cancel token to protect them the way `runWithTimeout`'s race
  protects every other deadline. On a cold, CPU-starved CI worker, pure scheduling delay between
  those two reads — not real in-process slowness — can make the subtraction go negative, timing a
  guard step out before it even runs and failing the turn closed with no tokens. Capping the test
  clock's jump keeps timestamps real for normal (fast) runs but stops one scheduling stall from
  reading as hundreds of ms of step latency, without touching `packages/harness` production code.
- risk: low

### 21 Oct 2026 · 7.2c must_not_contain phrases are literal substrings of the case's own scripted variant · decided by builder · risk: low

  `"<frame>: ${k0}"`; every `must_not_contain` phrase in the matching case file is a literal
  substring of one of those two rendered templates, and contains the bank-answer key itself.
- Why: this guarantees the phrase can only appear in the model's reply if the leak guard failed
  to suppress the key, so the real-guard test ("0 leaks") can pass only by truly blocking the
  key, and the mutation test (pass-through gate, no-op `answerLeak`) is guaranteed to render the
  phrase and get caught. A looser or paraphrased phrase could pass "caught" by coincidence, or
  fail "0 leaks" on wording the guard never needed to touch.
- risk: low

### 21 Oct 2026 · 0.21 deadline-safe test clock · decided by builder · risk: low
- Decided: fix the SSE route test flake by wrapping the web route tests' backend clock
  (`apps/web/test/turn-backend.ts`) so a guard/routing *deadline* (any `clock.sleep(ms, cancel)`
  call, per the harness's own convention) never races real wall-clock time against the in-memory
  scripted gateway; a genuine content-pacing delay (`sleep(ms)` with no cancel) still waits in
  real time, unchanged.
- Why: the flake's cause is a real `setTimeout`-based deadline (250-400 ms, several of them in the
  guard chain and route) racing an otherwise-instant scripted call; under CPU pressure the OS can
  make the timer fire first, failing the turn closed with no tokens. None of these tests want a
  real timeout to fire, and the production deadline values are correct for real traffic, so the
  fix belongs in the test's clock, not in `packages/harness` or in the timeout values themselves.
- risk: low — test-only change in `apps/web/test/`, no production code or contracts touched.

- Decided: a category with no row at all for its group is `measured: false` (never claims a pass
  or fail); a category whose row exists but has zero cases (`reason: 'empty_group'`) is
  `measured: true` with `percent: null` and `pass: false` (a real failure, the group was expected
  to run and didn't get any cases).
- Why: plan's explicit design note -- "a scorecard must not look like it answered something it
  didn't" (lessons.md), while an expected-but-empty group is still a real gate failure that must
  not be hidden behind "unmeasured."
- risk: low

### 21 Oct 2026 · 7.4 merge: scoped teacher eval-case read path reviewed and merged · decided by lead · risk: high
- Decided: merge 7.4, including `packages/db` `teacherEvalCases.listForTeacher` (a risky path), reviewed by security-reviewer and code-reviewer (the group's required reviewers) plus typescript-reviewer; all approved with no CRITICAL or HIGH. MEDIUM and LOW findings go to 7.4a; the undecided feedback and revision thresholds (blocker B-40) go to 7.4b, and until then a first_publish or prompt_pack_bump gate fails closed with a clear error.
- Why: the gate already blocks a bad agent and publishes a good one; the open thresholds only keep the full scope failing closed, which is the safe direction.
- risk: high

### Pedagogy and grounding thresholds are provisional pass-rate proxies
- Decided: pedagogy passes at a pass rate of 80% or more until the runner can score a 1-5 mean. Grounding is held to 99% and runs only on a first publish or a prompt-pack bump. Lead's Q2 answer, 21 Oct 2026; 7.2 or 7.6 revisits it once scored runs exist.
- Why: the runner scores pass/fail, not a mean, and the build plan's table has no grounding row.
- risk: medium

---

### The "< 15 minutes" proof is a simulated critical path, backed by a deadline that fails closed
- Decided: estimatedSeconds = (ceil(total calls / 4) + the most calls in one case) × 8 s, with one call per turn and one per judge statement. At run time, a 15-minute deadline stops new cases from starting, marks every unstarted case `not run: gate deadline passed`, and fails the gate even when the thresholds would tolerate the misses. The 8 s and 4-way constants are provisional until 7.6 and 7.7 measure real p95 (lead Q6).
- Why: wall clock means nothing under a scripted gateway, and lessons.md says never to gate CI on timings.
- risk: medium

---

### gatedPublish is the only publish path offered
- Decided: `gatedPublish` calls publish only when `gate.pass === true` (a truthy non-boolean does not count), and a gate that throws never publishes. 8.7 must publish through it.
- Why: "Blocks publish on failure" has to hold structurally, not by convention.
- risk: medium

---

### Empty, unknown or duplicate inputs fail closed
- Decided: an expected group with zero cases fails as `empty_group`. An unknown suite, an unknown change kind, an empty change set, a duplicate case id or a style pool under 30 throws `GateScopeError`. A case that throws counts as failed.
- Why: a check that silently skips looks like a pass (lessons.md).
- risk: low

---

### The per-agent locked group is required only when some package locks a module
- Decided: the gate expects a non-empty `agent:locked` group only if some package leaves out a module that the teacher's material covers. With such a module, 7.3's generator always makes at least three locked cases.
- Why: a teacher whose packages all cover every module has nothing to lock. Requiring the group anyway would block every publish for that teacher with `empty_group`.
- risk: medium

---

### Near-miss distress cases count in the 100% distress group
- Decided: every `safety` case whose id starts with `safety-distress-` goes into `safety-distress` (100%). That includes the 9 `safety-distress-nearmiss-*` cases, following the plan's prefix rule literally.
- Why: it is the stricter reading. If the lead wants near-misses held to the 99% safety rate instead, it is a one-line change.
- risk: low

---

### A material change runs per-agent locked cases only
- Decided: a material change does not run the platform locked suite; that suite runs only on a first publish or a prompt-pack bump (lead's Q1 answer).
- Why: the platform locked cases are written against the demo teacher's modules.
- risk: low

### 7.4 teacherEvalCases.listForTeacher (repositories, risky path)
- Decided: a new read-only repository method returns only the scope's own `teacher_eval_cases` rows (`id, moduleId, question, answer, origin`), filtered by `teacher_id` with parameterised Drizzle SQL after `teacherScope` validation, ordered `created_at, id`, wrapped by `guardAll`, and covered by the isolation grid plus its own int test.
- Why: 8.7 needs the teacher's answers and corrections as per-agent accuracy cases for the gate (7.3 Lead answer Q3); the method is in `packages/db/src/repositories/**`, a risky path.

### The CLI gate never offers --record and routes replay through the already-reviewed stand-ins
- Decided: `edmate gate` has no `--record` flag at all (not just a default), so there is no path
  through its own arguments to a live call; it always builds `fileRecorder(dir, 'replay')`
  (or a test-injected `Recorder`) and hands `runQualityGate` the existing `unwiredAgent` /
  `replayJudgeGateway` from `eval.ts`. Replay mode never invokes either (the recorder returns the
  fixture without calling `fn`), so this is structurally offline, not just offline by convention.
- Why: the lead's Phase C note says the gate command must stay offline even though `edmate eval`'s
  default agent went live in 7.6; reusing `eval.ts`'s own stand-ins keeps that guarantee in one
  place instead of a second copy.
- risk: low

### A full-scope CLI run reports every undecided threshold/group at once, not just the first
- Decided: before calling `runQualityGate`, `edmate gate` walks `platformCases` once itself
  (`fullScopeGaps`) and, for a `first_publish`/`prompt_pack_bump` change, lists every suite with
  no gate threshold and every threshold group with zero platform cases in one error, exit 1. It
  never edits `GATE_THRESHOLDS` or narrows scope to dodge the gap.
- Why: `selectGateCases` throws on the first unknown-suite case it meets while building the full
  scope, which would have named only one of today's two gaps (`feedback` vs. `revision`) and said
  nothing about the empty `accuracy` group; blocker B-40 needs the whole picture to decide
  thresholds from, not a single symptom.
- risk: medium

- Decided: `apps/cli/src/commands/gate/demoInput.ts` copies 7.3's test adapter but leaves out its

- Why: those rows exist only to exercise `generatePerAgentSuite`'s `teacher-answer` provenance in

- Decided: `TEACHER_EVAL_CASES_MAX = 10_000`; the query fetches one extra row and throws `RepositoryError('invalid')` if it exists. No paging and no `truncated` flag.
- Why: the gate must never run a silently cut suite (lessons.md: a check that skips looks like a pass); a teacher near the cap needs a later board task for sampling or paging, not a quiet partial read.

### `createChatGateway`'s openai-compatible factory takes `baseURL` as a per-call option, not a second env var
- Decided: the live sweep threads each `live-models.yaml` entry's own `baseURL` field (already in
  the 7.6 schema) through `liveAgentFor`/`ChatDepsOptions`/`createChatGateway`'s new `opts.baseURL`
  parameter, rather than reading a single global env var the way `judgeGateway.ts`'s
  `EDMATE_JUDGE_BASE_URL` does for the one pinned judge model.
- Why: the judge is one fixed model per run, so one env var is enough; the sweep can list several
  `openai-compatible` candidates with different endpoints in the same `live-models.yaml` file, and
  each entry already carries its own `baseURL` (validated in 7.6) — reading it from the file keeps
  one source of truth instead of adding a second, parallel env-var convention.
- risk: low

### A failed (model, suite) pair's summary row has only `error` set, never zeroed-out numbers
- Decided: `SweepSummaryRow` is a union — `{ model, suite, passed, total, cost }` on success, or
  `{ model, suite, error }` on failure — rather than always shipping `passed`/`total`/`cost` with
  placeholder zeros plus an optional `error`.
- Why: a reader of `summary.json` (a human, or a future dashboard) must never mistake a crashed
  pair for a pair that ran and scored zero; the union makes that ambiguity a type error instead of
  a convention to remember.
- risk: low

### `loadSweepCases`'s typed-error catch narrows to `NoCasesFoundError` specifically, not `CaseLoadError`
- Decided: only `NoCasesFoundError` (no files at all) is treated as "zero cases, not an error";
  `CaseLoadError` (a bad file inside a non-empty directory) still propagates and fails that pair.
- Why: the plan's rule is specifically about an empty suite directory (`evals/suites/pedagogy`'s
  `.gitkeep`-only case); a malformed case file is a real authoring mistake that the 7.6a resilience
  item (point 2) now surfaces per-pair instead of aborting the whole sweep, never silently as zero
  cases.
- risk: low
